content:
Apple has officially reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company. The company's stock price rose 17 points this week, surpassing Nvidia in Friday's intraday trading.

Apple's market capitalisation is steadily approaching the $5 trillion mark, with its share price having touched the $4.9 trillion level. Previously, Nvidia had become the first company to break through the $5 trillion market cap threshold.

Apple's stock price movement on Friday extended the company's recent string of record-breaking highs over the past few days.

Apple had earlier experienced a brief dip in its stock price after it unusually raised prices on Mac, iPad and other products due to the ongoing global memory shortage. However, after a full week of trading, the stock price has fully recovered its losses and rebounded.

The company's next milestone will be breaking through the $5 trillion market capitalisation mark.

On another note, Apple is undergoing a CEO transition, moving from Tim Cook to John Ternus. The announcement was officially made earlier this year, with August being the final month of Cook serving as Apple's CEO. He will remain in the role of Executive Chairman of the Board.
